status_summary: Two of the Mandate's specific steps are operative. Executive Order 14152 (signed 2025-01-20) directed the DNI to revoke the clearances of a named group of former intelligence and national security officials and of John Bolton, and DNI Gabbard announced on 2025-08-19 that she was revoking the clearances of 37 current and former officials; these actions name individuals rather than adopting the Mandate's general rule tied to unapproved public statements. On the leak side, Attorney General Bondi's memorandum of 2025-04-25 revoked Garland's July 2021 media-records policy (as described in the preamble of the Justice Department rule), and a final rule restoring a 2014-style version of 28 CFR 50.10 took effect 2025-05-02. On analysis, CIA Director Ratcliffe declassified an internal tradecraft review of the 2016 election assessment (2025-07-02) and, with the Attorney General, the Durham appendix (2025-07-31), and CIA announced on 2026-02-20 that Ratcliffe retracted or substantially revised 19 finished products after a review by the President's Intelligence Advisory Board and an internal review. A consolidated DNI and Attorney General audit, Hatch Act coverage for retirees, a National Intelligence University course, and pension forfeiture for convicted leakers were not found.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14152 (published 2025-01-29, 90 FR 8343) directs the DNI to revoke the clearances of named former intelligence and national security officials connected to a 2020 letter about the Biden family laptop story, and of John Bolton, and to report within 90 days on related IC conduct and on keeping the IC out of domestic elections.

Attorney General Bondi issues a memorandum revoking Attorney General Garland's July 19, 2021 memorandum limiting compulsory process against journalists; the preamble of the Justice Department's later rule says the 2022 amendments to 28 CFR 50.10 unduly hindered efforts to subpoena journalists who coordinated with federal employees to leak protected materials.
DOJ publishes a final rule amending 28 CFR 50.10 that rescinds the November 2022 amendments and restores a revised version of the 2014 regulation, effective on publication.

CIA Director Ratcliffe declassifies an internal lessons-learned review of the analytic tradecraft used in the 2016 election intelligence community assessment. Per CIA's page, the review identified a rushed schedule, unequal access to compartmented information, a sidelined National Intelligence Council and heavy involvement by agency heads, and Ratcliffe released it to promote analytic objectivity and transparency.

The Justice Department releases the declassified appendix to the Durham report, with CIA coordinating the declassification, and transmits it to Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley; Ratcliffe characterizes its contents as showing a coordinated effort against the incoming administration (an official characterization, not a finding).

DNI Gabbard confirms that she has revoked the security clearances of at least 37 current and former national security officials through a DNI memo circulated to intelligence agencies the previous day; the memo cited politicization or weaponization of intelligence, failures to protect classified information and unprofessional tradecraft. CNN and Defense One reported that no specific evidence was cited.

CIA announces that Director Ratcliffe has retracted or substantially revised 19 finished intelligence products, citing departures from analytic tradecraft standards and from independence from political considerations. The announcement says a President's Intelligence Advisory Board review of hundreds of finished CIA reports from the past decade and an internal review led by the Deputy Director reached the same findings; it does not mention the 2016 election assessment or the IC Analytic Ombudsman.

title: Revoke clearances, pursue leaks, and correct politicized intelligence analysis
uncertainties: The Attorney General's 2025-04-25 memorandum itself was not read; its date and effect are taken from the preamble of the Justice Department's final rule (90 FR 18785), which does not give it a formal title. The CIA announcements of 2025-07-02, 2025-07-31 and 2026-02-20 were read on cia.gov. ODNI's newsroom listing for August 2025 (pages covering 2025-07-22 to 2025-08-20) shows no release about the clearance revocations, so the 37-person revocation of 2025-08-19 still rests on news reports (CNN and Defense One) and the DNI memo itself was not located. A 2025-09-25 NBC News report of a Justice Department investigation of a former CIA director rested on unnamed administration officials and is not treated as an event. EO 14152 section 3(a) names 50 individuals (49 letter signatories plus Bolton), confirmed on federalregister.gov on 2026-10-26. Any court challenge to clearance revocations was not found. DOJ leak prosecutions, referrals by ODNI or CIA, and leak-related firings in 2025 and 2026 were not sourced and are left out. The ODNI report 'Personnel Vetting Trust Determinations' (2026-06-08) was not reviewed. The CIA retraction page says nothing about the IC Analytic Ombudsman, and no public report under the 90-day provision of EO 14152 was found. Rechecked 2026-10-26: searches found no new executive order, rule or DNI or CIA action on clearances, leaks or analytic politicization after the CIA announcement of 2026-02-20, and no primary ODNI page for the 2025-08-19 revocations (the announcement is known only from news reports). A news report (AOL, dated 2025-10-07) describes a DNI memo asking agencies to study polygraph feasibility and to add leak questions to screening; its issue date is not stated, so it is an unverified lead and not an event. The Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press analysis, an advocacy source, was removed as a source and no claim rests on it.
